surfaces.part: scrap heap mound (piled sheets, pipes, car parts)

answer.evidence: The object is an irregular dome-shaped heap of debris, wider at the bottom (46 px) and tapering to the top (rows 6-14). The upper rows show a sloping mound with a lighter orange corrugated sheet at rows 11-15 and a grey pipe band at rows 14-18, which function as upper surfaces seen from above. Below, the front face (rows ~19-30) holds a blue sheet, a wheel rim and a tyre drawn face-on. As debris it is an irregular heap, so there is no strict box top, but the heap's top slope and the sheet planes give a top surface of about 5 rows above a front face of about 14 rows.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate measures 18 visible tones per 16x16 tile. That is level with the stall (17) and the well (20) and well above the hedge (9). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted: dark rust-brown and blue-grey against the adjacent material, not a black sticker line. By eye, the heap reads as separate materials: corrugated sheet bands, a tyre, a rim and pipes, each with 3-4 tone steps and highlight/rust speckle. Its 26 total colours are fewer than the stall and well (38-40), and its material ramps are a little shallower than Beodeul's 5-6 steps. Its density per tile is still on par with the references, and the silhouette is varied and not a flat sticker. It would sit acceptably beside the references.
